Without Accessibility, Monorail can arrange the windows of apps such as Safari, Finder and Terminal by asking them to move their windows. With “Save browser tabs and Finder windows” on, it also asks your browser and Finder which tabs and folders are open, so snapshots can reopen them. And it reads and adds Apple Notes for the Notes tab, only when you open it. Nothing leaves this Mac.
Voice commands, which listen only while you hold the voice command, and Meeting Notes, which listen only while you record a meeting. Everything stays on this Mac.
Voice commands are turned into text on this Mac to arrange your windows, and Meeting Notes are transcribed on this Mac while you record a meeting.
The camera tile shows you during calls, and head focus (if you turn it on) watches which display you face. Nothing is recorded or sent.
Monorail's phone remote and layout sync with a nearby Mac use your local network.
Monorail reads the name of your Wi-Fi network to switch profile or layout when you join it. Your location is never stored or sent anywhere.
